Issues.Body:
Run the test, build and lint steps of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` through

Issues.Title: HttpParams.has() returns true and get() returns undefined for empty arrays
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

### Bug

Hi Angular team! When a search filter has no selected tags, passing `tag: []` to `HttpParams` makes `has('tag')` return `true` and `get('tag')` return `undefined`. The serialized URL omits `tag`.

### Minimal reproduction

```ts
import { HttpParams } from '@angular/common/http';

const params = new HttpParams({ fromObject: { tag: [], page: 1 } });

params.has('tag');  // Actual: true      Expected: false
params.get('tag');  // Actual: undefined Expected: null
params.toString();  // 'page=1'
```

### Cause and possible fix

The constructor stores the empty array in the `fromObject` branch. `has()` finds the key, and `get()` reads the missing first element. Skipping empty arrays would match `appendAll()`. [Relevant code in params.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/common/http/src/params.ts#L165-L198)

Issues.Title: refactor: remove selectorless and signal components prototypes
Issues.Body:
Removes two unfinished prototypes: selectorless template syntax and signal components. One commit each.

### refactor(compiler): remove selectorless prototype
- **compiler:** removes the component/directive lexer tokens, the `selectorlessEnabled`/`enableSelectorless` parse options, the html and R3 `Component`/`Directive` AST nodes and their visitor methods, direct pipe references in the expression parser, and the binder's selectorless directive matching (`referencedDirectiveExists`). Also removes the type-check ops (`ops/selectorless.ts`) and their out-of-band diagnostics, and the selectorless indexer identifier kinds.
- **compiler-cli:** removes `_enableSelectorless`, the selectorless component analysis and scope (`SelectorlessScope`), selectorless deferred deps, the selectorless template symbols, and the linker option. Error codes 2024, 2025, 2026 and 8018 were only used by selectorless and are deleted (the error_code API golden is updated).
- **hybrid preprocessor:** removes the selectorless analysis, TCB and indexer paths, the selectorless language-service symbol kinds, and the selectorless golden. The Rust `error_code.rs` is updated to match.
- **language-service:** removes selectorless definitions, quick info, references and rename, and the `enableSelectorless` plugin option.
- **core:** removes the `acceptance/selectorless` runtime tests and the schematic's `enableSelectorless` flag.

`SelectorlessMatcher` is **kept**. Foreign components (`foreignImports`) use it to match elements by tag name, and all `foreignImports` behaviour and tests are unchanged.

### refactor(core): remove signal components prototype
- `@Directive`/`@Component` no longer accept the internal `signals` option.
- ngtsc, JIT, the linker and the preprocessor no longer read `signals`. The compiler no longer emits `signals: true` in definitions, `isSignal: true` in partial declarations, or the trailing `IsSignal` type argument of `ɵɵDirectiveDeclaration`/`ɵɵComponentDeclaration` (that type parameter is removed).
- Removes `DirectiveDef.signals`/`ComponentDef.signals`, `LViewFlags.SignalView` (the later flag bits are renumbered) and the internal `ComponentMirror.isSignal`.
- Removes the `components_and_directives/signals` compliance case and updates the preprocessor `signals`/`advanced_signals` goldens.

Signal inputs, model inputs and signal queries (input- and query-level `isSignal`) are unaffected.

### Notes
- A few `@angular/compiler` internals change shape: the `html.Element`/`t.Element`/`t.Template`, `BindingPipe` and `Parser` constructors, and the `IdentifierKind` values.
- Two preprocessor language-service specs in `definitions_spec` ("matches more than one") failed depending on test order once the shards changed. They now call `env.openFile`, the same way their signal-input sibling spec does.

### Testing
`pnpm bazel test //packages/compiler/... //packages/compiler-cli/... //packages/language-service/... //packages/core/... //packages/localize/... //packages/forms/... //packages/common/... //goldens/...`: 583/585 targets pass, and `cargo test` passes in `ng-analyze`. The remaining failures are timing-sensitive browser specs (animations, `@defer` minimum, viewport scroller) in `common:test_web_firefox`, `core/test/acceptance:acceptance_web_firefox` and `acceptance/authoring:test_jit_web_chromium`. Each fails on some runs and passes on others: the two Firefox targets also fail some runs on `main` at e25a22841a, and `test_jit_web_chromium` passed 6/6 when rerun on this branch.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): length-prefix string literals and quoted map keys in ConstantPool keys
Issues.Body:
Previously, `GenericKeyFn.keyOf()` wrapped string literals and quoted object literal keys in double quotes without length-prefixing or escaping. As a result, distinct array or object literals extracted during the template compiler's pure function optimization phase (`generatePureLiteralStructures` / `extractPureFunctions` -> `PureFunctionConstant` in `ConstantPool`) such as `["a", "b"]` vs `['a","b']` or `{"a": 1, "b": 2}` vs `{'a":1,"b': 2}` produced identical constant pool keys (`["a","b"]` and `{"a":1,"b":2}`) and erroneously shared the same constant factory.

This change prefixes string literals and quoted object literal keys with their length (`"${value.length}:${value}"`) in `GenericKeyFn.keyOf()`. This guarantees a prefix-free (uniquely decodable) key encoding with O(1) overhead and avoids scanning or escaping characters via `JSON.stringify()`.

Fixes #71914

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): clear un-fingerprinted preprocessor cache and lazy parser closures
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Follows up on #71904:

1. In `HybridCompiler.invalidateStaleFileAnalysis`, moving `existing.boundFingerprint = nextFingerprint` outside the clearing `if` block while keeping `existing.boundFingerprint !== undefined && existing.boundFingerprint !== nextFingerprint` allows an un-fingerprinted `fileCache` entry (`boundFingerprint === undefined`, such as one populated by a direct `processFileSync` call) to be stamped with a valid `boundFingerprint` without clearing stale `parsedTemplates`, `preparedTcbData`, or `tcb` when a dependency's `<ng-content>` selectors change. Similarly, `populateBoundData` did not reset `fileAnalysis.tcb`, leaving stale TCB text for `getTcbForFile` when re-binding an un-fingerprinted entry.
2. In `parseComponentTemplate`, the lazy `diagNodes` getter shared `parseComponentTemplate`'s closure context, keeping the containing `.ts` file `content`, `ComponentMetadata`, and parse options alive on cached `ParsedComponentTemplate` entries even for external templates and even after `diagNodes` had already been evaluated.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

1. `HybridCompiler.invalidateStaleFileAnalysis` compares `existing.boundFingerprint !== nextFingerprint` directly so transitioning from `undefined` to a computed fingerprint clears stale cached state before stamping `nextFingerprint` (while keeping `(undefined, undefined)` intact), and `populateBoundData` clears `fileAnalysis.tcb = undefined` whenever `preparedTcbData` is recomputed.
2. `parseComponentTemplate` isolates the lazy `diagNodes` parser closures into `createInlineDiagParser` and `createExternalDiagParser` (avoiding capturing `ComponentMetadata`, and avoiding capturing `.ts` `content` for external/indirect templates) and `defineLazyDiagNodes` clears the parser closure reference once `diagNodes` is evaluated.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: compiler: interpolation ends early when a regular expression literal contains }}
Issues.Body:
### Bug

Hi Angular team! Angular treats `}}` inside a regular expression literal as the end of an interpolation.

### Minimal reproduction

```html
{{ /[}}]/u.test('}') }}
```

Expected `true`. Actual `Unexpected closing block`. The same expression fails in a `title` interpolation with `Unterminated regular expression` but parses successfully in a property binding. The equivalent pattern `/[}]/u` also parses in interpolation. AOT compilation with `ngc` reports `NG5002` for `{{ /}}/.test('}}') }}`.

### Cause and possible fix

The scanners appear to treat `}}` inside the regex as a closing delimiter. A possible fix is to skip regex literal contents while preserving division expressions such as `{{ 6 / 2 }}`. [HTML lexer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/ml_parser/lexer.ts#L1280-L1334) · [Expression parser](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/expression_parser/parser.ts#L523-L537)

### Environment

Angular compiler 22.2.5, Node.js 24.22.2, macOS arm64. Regression status unknown.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "compiler: interpolation ends early when a regular expression literal contains }}" (#71915)

Issues.Title: fix(core): do not keep elements created after hydration for event replay
Issues.Body:
Please note that this fixes a **real** production issue; it wasn't found speculatively through AI code analysis.

In some of our applications, memory kept growing with event replay enabled. The page used more memory after every route change.

Event replay keeps every element that has an event listener, so it can replay early events on it later. After hydration, Angular clears this list once. But then it keeps adding new elements to it, and nothing reads them again. For example:

- A list with 100 rows, where each row has a `(click)` listener, adds 100 elements every time the list is shown again.
- After a route change, the elements of the old page stay in memory, together with their listeners and components.

Only elements that come from the server have a `jsaction` attribute, and only these elements can be replayed. With this fix, Angular does not keep other elements anymore. This works with and without incremental hydration.

Fixes #66506
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(core): do not keep elements created after hydration for event replay" (#71927)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): do not end interpolation early when a regex literal contains }}
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #71915

An interpolation ends early when a regex literal inside it contains `}}`, for example `{{ /[}}]/u.test('}') }}`. The template lexer (`_consumeInterpolation` in `packages/compiler/src/ml_parser/lexer.ts`) only tracks quotes and `//` comments while looking for the closing `}}`, so the `}}` inside the regex is mistaken for the end of the interpolation. The expression parser (`_getInterpolationEndIndex` / `_forEachUnquotedChar` in `packages/compiler/src/expression_parser/parser.ts`) has the same gap, which is the path hit by e.g. `title` interpolations.

## What is the new behavior?

Both scanners now skip over regex literals while looking for the end of an interpolation. Whether a `/` starts a regex literal or is a division operator is decided from the previous significant characters, mirroring `isStartOfRegex()` in the expression lexer (regex after an operator, `(`, `[`, `,` or `:` or at the start of the expression; division after a value such as an identifier, a number, `)` or `]`; `!` is treated as a negation vs. a non-null assertion the same way the expression lexer treats it). A regex is only skipped when a closing `/` is found on the same line, so an unterminated regex keeps its previous behavior instead of swallowing the rest of the template. Division is unaffected: `{{ 6 / 2 }}`, `{{ a / b }}` and `{{ /a/ / 2 }}` still parse as before.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

## Other information

Tests run (locally, with the repo's own spec files run under Jasmine via an esbuild bundle, since Bazel was not available in this environment):

- New tests fail on the unmodified code and pass with the fix: `ml_parser/lexer_spec.ts` ("should parse interpolation with a regex literal containing }}") and `expression_parser/parser_spec.ts` ("should parse interpolation with a regex literal containing }}", "should still treat a slash after a value as division in interpolation").
- Full spec files, 816 specs, 0 failures: `packages/compiler/test/ml_parser/lexer_spec.ts`, `ast_serializer_spec.ts`, `html_parser_spec.ts`, `html_whitespaces_spec.ts`, `inline_comment_spec.ts`, `packages/compiler/test/expression_parser/ast_spec.ts`, `lexer_spec.ts`, `parser_spec.ts`, `serializer_spec.ts`.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean for the two changed source files.
- The examples from the issue (`{{ /[}}]/u.test('}') }}` in text and in a `title` attribute, plus `{{ /}}/.test('}}') }}` and `{{ 6 / 2 }}`) parse through `HtmlParser` and `Parser.parseInterpolation` with no errors.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): gate synchronous preprocessor APIs on synchronous hosts
Issues.Body:
Asynchronous bundler hosts suspend module resolution and content loading across
pump turns, so synchronous `*_blocking` and `*Sync` entry points cannot run to
completion within a single call. Without explicit host gating, calling a
synchronous entry point against an asynchronous host either panics inside WASM
or starts an analysis stream that stalls mid-iteration.

Enforce `AnalysisHost::is_synchronous` inside `QueryEngine::block_on_query` and
add fallible `ensure_synchronous_host` checks to `Analyzer`'s synchronous core
helpers. Convert `WasmAnalyzer::get_metadata_for_file` and `read_resource` to
return `Result<Option<String>, String>` and expose `is_synchronous_host` on
WASM bindings so synchronous WASM calls fail cleanly with
`"synchronous APIs require a synchronous host"` instead of panicking.

Surface `isSynchronousHost` on `IAnalyzer` and `WasmAnalyzer`, separating
internal WASM mutation/template helpers so asynchronous entry points continue
working while `*Sync` entry points across `WasmAnalyzer`, `HybridCompiler`, and
`getIndexedComponentsSync` immediately throw when `isSynchronousHost` is
`false`. Behavior under `DefaultFsHost` is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): gate synchronous preprocessor APIs on synchronous hosts" (#71919)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): drive WASM getMetadataForFile through the preprocessor pump loop
Issues.Body:
Previously, `WasmAnalyzer.getMetadataForFile` delegated directly to
`getMetadataForFileSync`, which synchronously stepped the WASM query engine
to completion inside a single FFI call. When an asynchronous `AnalysisHost`
suspends module resolution or content loading across JavaScript round-trips,
blocking inside a single WASM export cannot yield back to the host.

Issues.Title: compiler: distinct array literals can share a constant pool key and produce incorrect results
Issues.Body:
### Bug

Hi Angular team! Two different array literals in the same template can share a constant pool key. The template compiles but returns the wrong result.

### Minimal reproduction

Use this as a component template:

```html
{{ ["a", "b"].length }}|{{ ['a","b'].length }}
```

Expected `2|1`. Actual `2|2` in JIT and AOT. Reversing the expressions in JIT produces `1|1` instead of `1|2`.

### Cause and possible fix

`GenericKeyFn.keyOf()` wraps strings in quotes without escaping embedded quotes, giving both arrays the same key. Returning `JSON.stringify(expr.value)` in the string branch produced the expected result in local JIT and AOT tests. [Relevant code in constant_pool.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/constant_pool.ts#L247-L259)

### Environment

Angular compiler 22.2.5, Node.js 24.22.2, macOS arm64. Regression status unknown.

Issues.Title: Claude Code and Codex plugin marketplace for the agent skills in skills/dev-skills
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

None of them; this is about the agent skills in `skills/dev-skills`, which are published to https://github.com/angular/skills. That repo's README sends feedback to this tracker.

### Description

Angular already ships agent skills in `skills/dev-skills` (published to `angular/skills`): `angular-developer`, `angular-new-app`. 

What I couldn't find is a one-command install for Claude Code or Codex. Both can install a plugin from a git repository that carries a small marketplace file, and the file can point at skills a repo already has, so nothing needs copying or maintaining twice.

**Proposal:** add `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root, along these lines:

```json
{
  "name": "angular",
  "owner": {
    "name": "Angular"
  },
  "description": "Angular agent skills",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "angular",
      "source": "./skills/dev-skills",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./angular-developer",
        "./angular-new-app"
      ],
      "description": "Angular agent skills for Claude Code"
    }
  ]
}
```

Then `claude plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>` followed by `claude plugin install angular@angular` installs the skills. Codex has its own marketplace file (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, documented at https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins/build) and could be added the same way if you want it.

**What I checked:** I validated and installed exactly this manifest in Claude Code against a stand-in folder with the same layout and placeholder `SKILL.md` files named like yours; `claude plugin details` listed all 2 skills. Separately I installed Chakra UI's real `skills/` through a different marketplace with a `git-subdir` source, and its three skills appeared with no change to Chakra's repo. I only read each skill's front matter and README to judge that they are meant for end users.

If you'd rather not carry a marketplace file, tell me and I won't pursue it. I'm not offering a PR unless you ask for one.

<sub>Drafted with Claude Code.</sub>

### Proposed solution

A `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` as above, in whichever location flows to `angular/skills` through your publishing setup. I don't know how that output is generated, so I haven't guessed at the path.

### Alternatives considered

Keeping `npx skills add https://github.com/angular/skills` as the only install route, which works for tools that read that format but is not a one-command install inside Claude Code or Codex.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/pwa): add the manifest link when the index option is an object
Issues.Body:
The application and browser builders accept the `index` option either as a string or as an `{ input, output }` object. `ng add @angular/pwa` only collects string values when looking for index files to update, so a project using the object form gets no `<link rel="manifest">` tag. The failure is silent: when the object points at a custom file such as `src/app-index.html`, no index file is updated at all, and the installed application never loads the web app manifest.

Collect the `input` path of an object-form `index` alongside the string form, for both the target options and each configuration.

The new spec fails without the fix: with
`"index": { "input": "projects/bar/src/app-index.html", "output": "index.html" }`, the schematic left `app-index.html` without the manifest link.

<details>

### [`v31.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/releases/tag/v31.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/compare/v30.1.3...v31.0.0)

##### Breaking changes

- Changed the optional canvas and image decoding backend from `canvas` to `@napi-rs/canvas`. Install `@napi-rs/canvas` v1.0.13 or later in the v1.x series alongside jsdom; installing `canvas` alone no longer enables this support. The new backend provides prebuilt Skia binaries on supported platforms, and rendering and encoded image bytes can differ. Projects using native canvas objects or custom font registration should follow the [canvas migration guidance](https://redirect.github.com/jsdom/jsdom/blob/v31.0.0/README.md#canvas-support). Added WebP serialization through `canvas.toDataURL()` and `canvas.toBlob()`. Fixed image loading to wait for decoding before firing `load`, discard obsolete source requests, avoid refetching when dimensions change, and prevent failed images from drawing stale contents. Fixed canvas context and serialization behavior, including unsupported context types, read-only `ctx.canvas`, image-drawing exceptions, MIME type and quality normalization, and asynchronous `null` results from `canvas.toBlob()` for empty canvases or encoding failures. ([@​Brooooooklyn](https://redirect.github.com/Brooooooklyn))
- Changed CSS parsing, selector matching, and computed styles to use a new integrated implementation, with substantially expanded support and faster selector queries and repeated style reads. This includes cascade layers, nesting, `@scope`, custom-property substitution and registration through `@property` and `CSS.registerProperty()`, typed `attr()`, conditional `if()`, shadow-tree styling with `:host`, `::slotted()`, and `::part()`, pseudo-element computed styles, and constructable stylesheets with `document.adoptedStyleSheets` and `shadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets`. Fixed numerous cascade, shorthand, serialization, and default-style issues; computed declarations now stay live across DOM and stylesheet changes. CSS serialization and computed values can differ from previous releases.
- Changed HTML and XML parsing to pause at blocking scripts until their required resources are ready. The `JSDOM` constructor, `JSDOM.fromURL()`, and `JSDOM.fromFile()` can now return partially parsed documents. Wait for `DOMContentLoaded` for the finished tree, or the window's `load` event for load-delaying resources, checking `document.readyState` first in case the event has already fired. XML syntax errors encountered after asynchronous parsing resumes are reported through the virtual console as `"xml-parsing"` errors.

##### Other changes

- Added `window.reportError()`, which dispatches an `error` event and reports uncanceled errors to the virtual console. ([@​sarankumar1325](https://redirect.github.com/sarankumar1325))
- Added `element.ariaBrailleLabel` and `element.ariaBrailleRoleDescription`. ([@​Kjubikstronk](https://redirect.github.com/Kjubikstronk))
- Fixed page-completion `load` events to fire only on the window. Use `window.addEventListener("load", ...)` or `window.onload` instead of listening on the document.
- Fixed `document.open()`, including implicit calls from `document.write()`, to clear event listeners and handlers from the document, its descendants, and its window when replacing the input stream.
- Fixed `document.write()` to process successive writes through the parser's input stream, preserve insertion points across nested scripts, and make completed text immediately visible. Script-created input streams now remain open until `document.close()`.
- Fixed dynamically inserted scripts to respect `script.async = false` execution order, use their source text and document from preparation time, and avoid executing after adoption into another document. Scripts parsed through inert fragment APIs no longer execute when subsequently inserted.
- Fixed unrelated images, stylesheets, and frames being delayed behind scripts, and resource completion events firing before nested stylesheet imports finish. Cyclic imports no longer prevent completion, and `<style>` elements in shadow trees now fire `load` events.
- Fixed `window.stop()` to cancel pending subresource and `XMLHttpRequest` requests in descendant frames and suppress completion events for canceled loads, while allowing subsequent requests to proceed.
- Fixed repeated `document.close()` calls replaying readiness and load events, and incorrect iframe load events when reopening documents from event handlers.
- Fixed memory leaks where pending request interceptor promises retained closed windows, introduced in v28.0.0.
- Fixed focus remaining on elements that become non-focusable after DOM or style changes. Focus now moves asynchronously to the document's viewport, and `element.blur()` can release it immediately.
- Fixed `document.hasFocus()` returning false before an element is focused or during focus transitions within the document, including inside frames.
- Fixed `<template>` parsing and `template.innerHTML` serialization in XML documents, including templates with namespace prefixes. ([@​b84330808](https://redirect.github.com/b84330808))
- Fixed `rect.toJSON()` and `performance.toJSON()` to create their result objects in the method's realm instead of the host Node.js realm.

Issues.Body:
When `ng update` aborts because a package uses the `catalog:` protocol, the manual migration steps hardcode pnpm and yarn: the install step suggests 'pnpm install' for every package manager except yarn, and the catalog file hint only names pnpm-workspace.yaml and .yarnrc.yml. The previous generic text is kept as a fallback when the package manager is unknown.

The new spec fails without the fix: with `packageManager: 'bun'`, the guidance suggested 'pnpm install' and the pnpm/yarn file names.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve component initialization in Karma test bundles
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (not applicable: internal Karma bundling fix; no new options or public API)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Fixes #34250.

With `@angular/build:karma`, a component imported through a barrel can be captured as `undefined` in another component's `imports` array. This depends on the combination of spec entry points: an async spec importing the component directly can cause lazy module initialization to cross shared-chunk boundaries. The consuming decorator can run before the component is initialized.

The regression fixture includes:

1. A standalone layout component re-exported by a barrel.
2. A dialog importing that barrel and used by two specs.
3. A page importing the barrel and used by another spec.
4. An async spec importing the layout directly.

Against main (`2c6e8b970`), the browser reports **2 failed, 2 successful**. Both dialog specs throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ɵcmp')`.

## What is the new behavior?

The Karma build routes the discovered spec entry points through a shared virtual module that imports all selected specs. This keeps spec initialization in one module graph, avoiding the problematic partitioning across independent spec entry points.

- Preserve the existing `spec-*` entry names, including basename-collision handling.
- Keep code splitting enabled so Angular and its testing environment remain shared with the setup entry point.
- Include the original spec files as TypeScript root files, since the build entry points now refer to the virtual module.
- Preserve `include`/`exclude` selection: the virtual module only imports the specs collected by the existing discovery logic.

The same four browser specs now all pass. The added integration test exercises real Karma/Chrome execution rather than only checking generated bundle text.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Simply setting `disableCodeSplitting: true`, as suggested by the earlier Vitest fix in #33729, was insufficient for Karma in this reproduction: it produced testing-environment initialization errors. This change retains shared framework chunks instead.

Validation on macOS arm64, Node.js 24.22.2, pnpm 12.16.1, and Chrome Headless 159:

- `pnpm bazel test //packages/angular/build:karma_integration_tests --config=no-sharding --test_output=errors`: **42 integration specs, 0 failures**.
- ESLint for the changed implementation passes. The repository ESLint configuration excludes builder integration fixtures.
- Prettier checks for both changed files and `git diff --check` pass.

The full repository and E2E suites were not run. Large-suite build size/performance and dynamic addition of spec files during watch mode were not separately benchmarked or validated.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve unaffected localized chunk URLs
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the [guidelines](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines)
- [x] Regression tests were added to the existing i18n suites
- [ ] Docs were updated (no public option changes)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

The application builder adds a digest of the translation files to every JavaScript bundle. Editing one locale can give unrelated chunks new URLs in every locale, forcing browsers to download them again.

Fixes #30675.

## What is the new behavior?

For one-shot browser builds with bundle hashing enabled, compute names after localization. A changed bundle gets a new URL, and bundles that reference it get updated URLs. Unchanged bundles retain their URLs. The dependency graph comes from the esbuild/Rolldown output metadata; JavaScript is parsed when references need to be rewritten or to find worker URLs that are absent from the graph.

Watch, server builds, and builds with custom code plugins keep the existing hashing path.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Measurements and verification

**Chromium 153, warm browser cache.** Changed one French XLF message used by a lazy chunk, switched deployments on the same origin, and opened the page and one independent lazy chunk. JS used immutable cache headers; HTML used `no-store`. All three runs per locale and variant gave the same results. Bytes are Brotli response bodies, excluding headers.

| Locale | JS responses (main → PR) | JS bytes downloaded (main → PR) |

Issues.Title: Debug ID changes the bytes of polyfills and main but not their file names, so cached files fail the SRI check
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

Yes. It started with the debug IDs in 22.1.0.

### Description

Follow-up to #34574.

The builder names `polyfills-<hash>.js` and `main-<hash>.js` first. Then it adds a `//# debugId=<id>` line to the file. It computes `<id>` from the source map after it rewrites the map to add `x_google_ignoreList`. The file name does not cover that line.

So when a builder release writes the source map differently, the JS bytes change and the file name stays the same. 22.1.8 did that. Commit 5a0d226b7c moved `x_google_ignoreList` to the start of the map.

With `subresourceIntegrity`, the new `index.html` pins the new bytes. A CDN or browser cache that kept the old file under the same URL serves the old bytes, and the browser blocks the script. This happened to us in production with `polyfills-<hash>.js`.

#34583 fixed this for the chunks of the chunk optimizer. It does not cover files that esbuild names, such as `main` and `polyfills`. 22.2.6 still computes their debug ID from the rewritten map.

### Minimal Reproduction

```bash
npx @angular/cli@22.1.8 new repro --defaults --ssr=false
cd repro
npm install zone.js
npm install -D @angular/build@22.1.6
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.options.polyfills '["zone.js"]'
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.configurations.production.sourceMap true
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.configurations.production.subresourceIntegrity true
npx ng build && mv dist/repro/browser ../build-22.1.6
npm install -D @angular/build@22.1.8
npx ng build && mv dist/repro/browser ../build-22.1.8
```

Both builds write `polyfills-QWJLBG44.js` and `main-HHND32NM.js`. In each file, only the `//# debugId=` line differs:

```
polyfills-QWJLBG44.js
  build-22.1.6: //# debugId=d932f97d-b667-5462-b3b7-b328a1ce7f5a
  build-22.1.8: //# debugId=81c8766a-7d41-50fd-ac6d-16c3c4ed6358
main-HHND32NM.js
  build-22.1.6: //# debugId=e3a30145-1442-57c2-96a7-a88f9bf43b0a
  build-22.1.8: //# debugId=50dd2d3c-f1e3-5224-9587-43f24f562421
```

The two `index.html` files pin different hashes for the same URLs. For both files, the two source maps have the same content in a different key order.

### Exception or Error

```
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource 'https://example.com/polyfills-JTOAPWZJ.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '...'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```
Angular CLI: 22.1.8
@angular/build: 22.1.6, then 22.1.8
@angular/core: 22.2.5
zone.js: 0.16.3
Node: 24.17.0
OS: macOS
```

### Anything else relevant?

Expected: when the bytes of a hashed file change, its name changes too.

A possible fix is to compute the debug ID from the JS before the builder adds the debug ID line, not from the rewritten map. The file name already covers the JS.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): add the missing vi import for toHaveBeenCalledBefore in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
The `toHaveBeenCalledBefore` transformation rewrites the matcher to a comparison of `vi.mocked(spy).mock.invocationCallOrder` values but never registers `vi` as a pending value import. When the schematic runs with `--add-imports`, the migrated file only imports `expect` and fails to compile with "Cannot find name 'vi'" unless another transformation in the same file happens to use `vi`.

Register the `vi` import when the matcher is transformed, as every other transformation that emits `vi.*` already does.

The new spec fails without the fix: the migrated output contained `import { expect } from 'vitest'` instead of `import { expect, vi } from 'vitest'`.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup
Issues.Body:
The karma builder schema documents the `poll` and `progress` options, but the application build it starts never receives them: `--no-progress` still logs build progress and `poll` does not switch the file watcher to polling. The legacy webpack-based karma builder honored both options.

Forward both values to the build options. No new test since both are pass-through options; the package unit tests cover the compilation of the changed setup.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup" (#34654)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`
Issues.Body:
In a Git worktree the development server keeps its Vite cache in the worktree's own cache directory while the configured path resolves to the shared cache of the main checkout. `ng cache clean` removes both since the `getCacheConfig` localPath addition, but `ng cache info` still reports only the shared path and its size, so the cache that the development server actually writes to in that checkout is invisible.

Print the local path and its size when it differs from the shared path. Outside of a worktree both paths are the same and the output is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`" (#34653)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): remove unused exports
Issues.Body: Remove the `export` keyword from four symbols that are only referenced within their defining file: `calculateThresholds` and `checkThresholds`, whose external callers moved to `checkBudgets` in 4d27c38cd4; `augmentAppWithServiceWorkerCore`, which is only called by the exported wrapper functions; and `getEntryPointName`, whose external call sites were removed in 75abe2cc52. The two threshold functions also leave the unsupported `private` entry point, which re-exports the bundle calculator module; neither `@angular-devkit/build-angular` nor `@angular/cli` references them, and both still compile. The public API golden is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(@angular/build): remove unused exports" (#34651)

Issues.Title: fix(material/slider): align slider thumb with cursor on Firefox during drag
Issues.Body:
#### Description
On Firefox, when clicking and dragging the slider thumb, the visual thumb was pulled closer to the center of the track than the cursor, especially visible near the ends of the slider track.

This occurred because `.mdc-slider__input` did not reset native range appearance or pseudo-elements (`::-moz-range-thumb` and `::-moz-range-track`). In Gecko's user-agent stylesheet, the native range thumb has a default width of `1.4em` (~22.4px) with border insets, whereas Angular's geometry calculation assumes a 16px knob diameter (`_knobRadius: 8`). This resulted in a dead-zone where Firefox's native drag coordinates lagged behind the mouse position.

This PR:
- Resets native appearance (`appearance: none`, `-moz-appearance: none`, `-webkit-appearance: none`) and clears background on `.mdc-slider__input`.
- Explicitly sizes `::-moz-range-thumb` to 16px to match `_knobRadius` and clears borders on `::-moz-range-track`.
- Adds unit test coverage asserting native appearance reset on the input element.

Fixes #34094

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/menu): use latest trigger data when menu is reopened
Issues.Body: Fixes #26256 `CdkMenuTriggerBase.getMenuContentPortal()` only creates a new `TemplatePortal` when `menuTemplateRef` changes. The portal captures `menuData` as its context when it's created, so changes to `cdkMenuTriggerData` / `cdkContextMenuTriggerData` were never picked up. The menu kept rendering with the data from the first time it was opened. This also compares `menuData` against the portal's context and recreates the portal when it's a different object. The portal is only read when the menu opens, so an already open menu doesn't change; the new data shows up the next time it's opened. That matches what the issue asks for. Mutating the same object in place keeps working as it does today, since the context is the same reference. ### Tests Added a "reopen with new data" spec for both `CdkMenuTrigger` and `CdkContextMenuTrigger`: open with `{message: 'Hello!'}`, close, switch to `{message: 'Goodbye!'}`, reopen. ``` bazel test //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` Without the change in `menu-trigger-base.ts` both new specs fail with `Expected 'Hello!' to be 'Goodbye!'.` ### Manual check Same setup as the issue's StackBlitz: `[cdkMenuTriggerData]="{counter: counter()}"`, open the menu, close it, click "Increment" twice, open it again (Chromium, CDK 22.2.6 and then the same build with this change): Before: the button says 2, the menu still says 0 After: the menu says 2

Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): ngMenuContent is never destroyed once the trigger has been focused, ignoring preserveContent
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

`ngMenu` hosts `DeferredContentAware` and exposes its `preserveContent` input, which defaults to `false`. So `ngMenuContent` should behave like `ngTabContent` and `ngAccordionContent`: rendered while the panel is visible, and destroyed when it hides.

It isn't. The menu computes the content's visibility as:

```ts
contentVisible = this._pattern.visible() || !!this.parent()?._pattern.hasBeenInteracted()
```

`hasBeenInteracted` is set to `true` in `onFocusIn` / `onKeydown` of `MenuTriggerPattern`, `MenuItemPattern`, `MenuPattern` and `MenuBarPattern`, and nothing ever sets it back to `false`. That has two effects:

1. **Content is built before the menu opens.** Tabbing onto the trigger (or onto a submenu's parent item) renders the deferred rows, even if the menu is never opened.
2. **Content is never destroyed afterwards.** Once the parent has been focused, `contentVisible` is `true` for the rest of the component's life, so `preserveContent: false` has no effect, through close, Escape, outside click and item selection alike.

For comparison, tabs and accordion set `contentVisible.set(this.visible())`, and their content is torn down when hidden.

Rendering a submenu's rows when its parent item gains focus looks intentional: it lets one ArrowRight move focus straight into the submenu. The problem is that the flag is sticky. Something like "parent is focused or active right now" would keep that benefit and still allow teardown.

**Why it matters:** the main reason to defer menu content is a menu repeated per row of a table or list. With the current behaviour, every menu the user has focused, even without opening it, keeps its rows for the life of the page, and `preserveContent` can't opt out of that.

### Reproduction

Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section **C**, with section **D** as the tabs control)

Steps:
1. Load the page. "Live rows C" reads **0**.
2. Tab onto "Open menu C" without opening it. "Live rows C" reads **2**.
3. Press Enter, then Escape. The menu closes, and "Live rows C" still reads **2**. The rows are never destroyed.
4. Control: in section D, switch tabs. Each panel's `ngTabContent` is created and destroyed as its tab is selected and deselected.

Probe log from the steps above:

```
D: "One" created
C: "Edit" created      ← trigger focused, menu not opened
C: "Delete" created
D: "One" destroyed
D: "Two" created
D: "Two" destroyed
D: "One" created
```

(No "C … destroyed" line at any point, including after closing the menu.)

### Expected Behavior

With `preserveContent` unset (`false`), `ngMenuContent` is destroyed when the menu hides, as `ngTabContent` and `ngAccordionContent` are. Ideally it's also not rendered merely because the trigger received focus. If eager rendering on parent focus is intended for submenus, it shouldn't make the content permanent.

### Actual Behavior

The content is rendered on the first `focusin` / `keydown` of the trigger or parent item and is never destroyed until the host view is.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- @angular/aria / @angular/cdk: 22.2.6 (also present in 22.2.5)
- Browser: Chromium 156
- OS: macOS

Issues.Title: bug(cdk/scrolling): nested viewports and overlay content inherit the outer `scrollWindow` / `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` scroller
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### Description

`scrollWindow` and `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` provide `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` through `providers`, and `CdkVirtualScrollViewport` takes it with `inject(VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, {optional: true})`. So every viewport below them in the injector tree uses the outer scroller, not just the viewport it was meant for:

- a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` nested in the rows of an outer virtual list that uses `scrollWindow` or `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`;
- a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` inside an overlay opened from such a row (`cdkConnectedOverlay`, and therefore also a virtual list inside a `mat-select` panel), even though the overlay isn't inside the scrolling element in the DOM at all.

Such an inner viewport never gets the `cdk-virtual-scrollable` class, so it can't scroll by itself. The mouse wheel scrolls the page or the outer element instead, the rendered range follows the outer scroller, and the rendered items spill out of the viewport box over the following rows.

The docs describe both options per viewport ("add the `scrollWindow` attribute to the `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport`"), and nothing says nested viewports inherit the scroller. As a workaround, `{provide: VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, useValue: null}` on a component between the two viewports makes the inner one scroll by itself again.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/7ytfjjia-a8v2qj79

It's the docs example "Virtual scrolling window" opened via "Edit in StackBlitz", with only the example file replaced.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open the StackBlitz. The outer list uses `scrollWindow`, and every row has its own 150px high virtual list with 100 items. The red line under each inner list already says it uses the outer scroller.
2. Hover an inner list and scroll with the mouse wheel: the page scrolls, the list doesn't.
3. The radio buttons at the top switch the outer list to `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` and move the inner list into a `cdkConnectedOverlay`. All four combinations are broken.
4. Select "its own viewport" to compare: the inner lists scroll by themselves.

### Expected Behavior

A viewport nested inside another virtual scroll viewport, or rendered in an overlay, scrolls by itself, the same way it does when the outer list uses its own viewport.

### Actual Behavior

The inner viewport uses the outer scroller (`viewport.scrollable !== viewport`) in all four combinations:

- `scrollWindow`, nested in a row: the wheel scrolls the page, the inner list renders ~40 items that overflow its 150px box and follow the page scroll.
- `scrollWindow`, in an overlay: the wheel scrolls the page instead of the list.
- `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`, nested in a row: the wheel scrolls the outer element.
- `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`, in an overlay: the list can't be scrolled at all and stays on its first 30 items, which overflow the panel.

With an outer list that scrolls itself, both placements work.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.5
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (same with 22.3.0-next.5)
- Browser(s): Chrome 157
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS 26

---

Not a regression: the scroller has been injected this way since `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` was added in #24394 (14.1.0). A possible direction: a viewport could act as a boundary for its content, so viewports and overlays declared inside it don't inherit an outer scrollable, and `scrollWindow` could apply only to its own host viewport.

We ran into this with Taiga UI dropdowns that use a virtual scroll inside virtualized lists (taiga-family/taiga-ui#10095).

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/menu): don't close menu until outside press is released
Issues.Body: Fixes #27878 With a standalone `cdkMenuTriggerFor`, pressing down anywhere outside the open menu closes it immediately, before the button is released. As noted in the issue, the outside click listener never gets a chance: the mousedown blurs the menu, `menuStack.hasFocus` emits `false` and `CdkMenuTrigger` calls `closeAll()`. That means the close can't be cancelled by moving the pointer away before releasing (WCAG 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation), and it's different from the menu bar and `mat-menu`. I didn't remove the `hasFocus` listener, because it's also what closes the menu when focus leaves it from the keyboard (Tab, or focus moving somewhere else programmatically). Instead, while a root menu is open the trigger now tracks pointer presses on the document: - `pointerdown` outside of the trigger and the menu stack marks that a press is in progress. - If focus leaves the menu during that press, closing is deferred until `pointerup`. - On `pointerup` the menu closes if the pointer was released outside, and stays open if it was moved back onto the menu. - `pointercancel` and closing the menu reset the state, and the listeners are only attached while the menu is open. I listen on the document rather than relying on the overlay's outside click events. A press on the empty area below a short page lands on ``, which the outside click dispatcher (attached to `body`) doesn't see, and the menu would stay open after the release. Focus loss that isn't caused by a press closes the menu right away, the same as before. ### Tests New specs in `menu-trigger.spec.ts` (standalone trigger): - focus leaving the menu without a press still closes it - press outside → focus leaves → menu stays open → `pointerup` outside closes it - press outside → focus leaves → `pointerup` on the menu keeps it open - a press that was already released doesn't stop focus loss from closing the menu ``` bazel test //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/cdk/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` Without the change in `menu-trigger.ts`, the two press specs fail (`Expected 1 to be 2.`). ### Manual check Standalone trigger + `cdkMenu` with a nested submenu, CDK 22.2.6 and then the same build with this change. I drove it with Playwright using real mouse events, holding the button for 500ms on the page background: | | Chromium 156 | Firefox 157 | WebKit 27.2 | |---|---|---|---| | menu open while the press is held (before → after) | no → yes | no → yes | no → yes | | closed after releasing outside | yes → yes | yes → yes | yes → yes | | press outside, drag back onto the menu, release | closed → stays open | closed → stays open | closed → stays open | | Tab out of the menu | closes → closes | closes → closes | closes → closes | Before, while the mouse button is still held down outside the menu: After:

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): activate interactive content inside menu items
Issues.Body:
### What does this PR do?

Menu items can wrap native interactive elements (a link, a button, an input), but
`Enter`/`Space` only ran the menu's selection logic. The wrapped element was never
activated, so link items and items with `(click)` handlers inside the content were
effectively mouse-only.

`MenuItemPattern` now resolves the interactive element rendered inside the item and
clicks it when the item is triggered. The click bubbles up to the menu's existing
`click` handler, so the item is still selected exactly as it is on a mouse click —
keyboard and mouse now behave the same. Items without interactive content keep their
current behavior, and menu bar items still open their submenu first.

Fixes #34072.

### Testing

- Added unit coverage in `src/aria/menu/menu.spec.ts` for a menu whose items wrap a
  link, a button, and no interactive content at all, asserting that `Enter` and
  `Space` activate the inner element and still report the selection.
- Type checking of the changed sources (`src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts` and
  `src/aria/menu/menu.spec.ts`) passes.
- Note: `bazel test //src/aria/menu:unit_tests` could not be run on my machine because
  Bazel fails to resolve the `rules_sass` toolchain on Windows, unrelated to this change.

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): activate the item element on enter and space
Issues.Body: Fixes #34072 The menu's keyboard manager prevents the default action for Enter and Space, and `MenuPattern.trigger()` only called `submit()`. So with the keyboard the item's element was never activated: `` didn't navigate and a `(click)` listener on the item didn't run. Both work with the mouse because the real click happens before the menu handles it. `trigger()` now calls `element.click()` on the active item (when it's enabled and doesn't open a submenu) and then submits, which is the same order a pointer click goes through. The synthetic click bubbles up to the menu's `(click)` host listener, so `onClick` ignores clicks while the item is being activated. Otherwise the item would be submitted twice and focus would jump back into the menu. Items with a submenu still just open the submenu, and disabled items still do nothing. ### Tests - `private/menu/menu.spec.ts`: Enter/Space clicks the element. Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): close only the focused submenu on escape
Issues.Body: Fixes #34071 Escape inside a nested `ngMenu` was calling `closeAll()`, so the whole menu tree closed and focus jumped back to the trigger. The APG menu pattern says Escape should close the menu that has focus and put focus back on whatever opened it, and that's also how `cdk/menu` and `mat-menu` already behave. I added a `closeCurrent()` on `MenuPattern` and pointed the Escape binding at it. If the menu is a nested submenu (its parent item isn't in a menubar), it closes just that submenu with `refocus: true`, the same path ArrowLeft/`collapse()` already uses. Otherwise it falls back to `closeAll()`, so first-level menus under a trigger or a menubar close exactly as before. ### Tests New specs: - `private/menu/menu.spec.ts`: Escape from a trigger's submenu, and from a nested submenu under a menubar menu - `menu/menu.spec.ts`: directive test using the existing Berries submenu. Escape from Blueberry leaves the main menu open and focuses Berries ``` bazel test //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_chromium PASSED //src/aria/private/menu:unit_tests_firefox PASSED ``` I also checked that the new tests fail without the change to `menu.ts` (all three fail with `Expected false to be true.`). ### Manual check I used the repro from the issue (https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro, section A): open menu A, go to Categorize, ArrowRight into the submenu, press Escape. The focused element is outlined in red. Before (22.2.6): both menus close and focus goes back to "Open menu A" After (same build with this change applied): the submenu closes, the root menu stays open and focus is on "Categorize" Ref: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/ (Escape: "Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to the element or context, e.g., menu button or parent menuitem, from which the menu was opened.")

Issues.Title: fix(material/form-field): support a different direction than the page
Issues.Body:
The form field styles used `[dir='rtl']` selectors, which match any ancestor with `dir="rtl"`. This meant that a form field with `dir="ltr"` inside an RTL page still got the RTL styles: the outline lost its leading border and the label, padding and native select arrow were placed for RTL.

These changes switch the styles to logical properties, so they follow the direction of the form field itself. `transform-origin` and `clip-path` have no logical equivalents, so those two rules use `:dir(rtl)`, which also resolves against the closest element with a `dir` attribute.

Measured in an Angular 22.2 / Material 22.2.6 app (Chromium and Firefox), label offset from the start edge of a `dir="ltr"` field inside a `dir="rtl"` page:

| | Before | After | Plain LTR page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outline | 29px | 16px | 16px |
| Fill | 65px | 52px | 52px |
| Native select | 33px | 16px | 16px |
| Outline leading border | 0px | 1px | 1px |

Fields in a plain RTL page measure the same before and after.

Fixes #26778.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/form-field): support a different direction than the page" (#34081)

Issues.Title: fix(material/list): use theme spacing for leading icons in RTL
Issues.Body:
In RTL, the leading icon of a list item had its margins hardcoded to `32px` and `16px`, instead of using the `leading-icon-start-space` and `leading-icon-end-space` tokens like in LTR. The rule has to use physical properties, because icon font stylesheets (e.g. Material Icons/Symbols) set `direction: ltr` on the icon, which makes the logical margins resolve as LTR inside an RTL list. With the M2 values (16px/32px) this happened to look correct, but with M3 (16px/16px, smaller with density) the gap between the icon and the text was twice as large in RTL.

These changes swap the token values in the RTL rule instead of hardcoding them, so RTL mirrors LTR for any theme.

Measured in an Angular 22.2 / Material 22.2.6 app (Chromium and Firefox), edge → icon / icon → text:

| Tokens | LTR | RTL before | RTL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| M3 default (16/16) | 16 / 16 | 16 / **32** | 16 / 16 |
| M3 density -2 (8/8) | 8 / 8 | **16 / 32** | 8 / 8 |
| M2 (16/32) | 16 / 32 | 16 / 32 | 16 / 32 |

Fixes #30537.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/list): use theme spacing for leading icons in RTL" (#34080)
